niche: an electric utility's company-owned LED streetlights: each conversion phase's share of luminaires still on their original driver whose driver will fail before the luminaire's twelfth year, read past a follow-up that ends early in the drivers' wear-out
answer: Put conversion phases P1, P3, P5, P7 and P9 into the 2027 group driver replacement program, 20,922 luminaires still on their original driver.
answer_source: task281/submission.md block 1; task281/generator/figures.json call.set and call.program_luminaires
analyst_test: A strong analyst who takes each luminaire's retrofit date from the installer's logs, every driver failure from both work-management systems, and fits the lifecycle model's two-parameter Weibull with suspensions to the whole conversion files every one of the ten phases into the 2027 group driver replacement program, against the golden's five, because the drivers from one of the two makers never show the wear-out and their zeros are read as failures still to come.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a lifetime distribution read past its follow-up under a censoring structure in which part of the suspensions are cures, not failures still to come: each phase's share of original-driver luminaires whose driver will fail before year twelve, from a Weibull fitted only to the drivers at risk of the wear-out; replacing it with the failure share to date, a constant annual rate or one fit over every luminaire files other phases, and no noun swap makes the cure structure appear.
layer1: the GIS register's install year is the pole's; each luminaire's retrofit date sits in the installer's daily logs
two work-management systems, the legacy one to June 2023 and its successor after, with different layouts and resolution codes
customer outage reports keyed by address and nearest pole, duplicated across the portal and the call centre
luminaires replaced after vehicle knockdowns carry a new serial and lot on an old pole
drivers replaced twice on one pole, the second on a stock driver
certificates of conformance per delivery lot as scanned PDFs, part numbers with revision suffixes
pole identifiers formatted differently in the GIS, the installer's logs and the work orders

driver: The decisive quantity is the share of each group's surviving units that will suffer one wear-out failure before a fixed age, read past a record whose follow-up ends early in the wear-out, when part of the units carry a part from a source that never wears out that way; the record is too young to show the plateau, so one lifetime fit on every unit passes its back-test and treats those units' zeros as failures still to come, and only a provenance record kept for warranty claims, joined unit by unit through the delivery lot, shows which units are at risk at all.
driver_concrete: Each conversion phase's share of luminaires still on their original driver on 1 January 2027 whose driver will fail before the luminaire's twelfth year comes from a Weibull fitted only to the drivers of the maker whose drivers wear out; the other maker's drivers, identified only through the installer's lot numbers and the manufacturer's certificates of conformance, show no wear-out, so one fit over every luminaire reads their zeros as failures still to come and puts every phase in the program.
stump: A competent solver fits the lifecycle model's Weibull with suspensions to every conversion driver and projects each phase's original-driver luminaires, filing all ten phases into the 2027 group driver replacement program at 68 to 71 per cent each; Corvane's drivers, found only through the installer's lot numbers and the luminaire maker's certificates of conformance, show no wear-out (16 failures against the 555 that fit expects), so the fit belongs to Vantrel's drivers alone and only P1, P3, P5, P7 and P9 clear 45 per cent.

differentiation.task141: task141 moves every unit to the rate the units already at a ceiling show under a cap; task281 has no policy change: it removes from the population at risk the units whose part source never shows the wear-out, found through a provenance record joined unit by unit, before a lifetime fit is read past its follow-up.
differentiation.task177: task177's architecture 3 reads a loan outcome as one rare event's rate times a conversion share, the event rare in the record and common forward; task281 has no event to convert: a censored lifetime fit's suspensions hold a sub-population whose part never wears out, found unit by unit through a provenance join, so each phase's at-risk share is built before the fit is carried past the follow-up.
differentiation.task301: task301 discounts each list by its own population's exit rate over its record ages; task281 discounts nothing by record age: it takes out of a censored lifetime fit the units whose part source shows no wear-out, found through the installer's lot and the maker's certificate, and projects the at-risk remainder to a fixed age.
differentiation.task75: task75 finds a second inflow channel as the residual between two counts of one period and projects it by its recurrence; task281 has no second channel or residual: it splits one lifetime record by the provenance of each unit's part and fits the wear-out to the source at risk alone.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is each group's need in a coming year read from an upper cut of its weekly shortfall distribution, rebuilt from last year's shortfalls with that year's own structural gaps replaced by the coming year's planned ones, and the added capacity rated at the availability of the newest members who will fill it; last year's weeks as they stood, or the group's average availability, each file other counts.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each unit's FY2028 relief positions are its fifth-heaviest week of backfill need over the weekly hours a relief officer works, the need built from FY2026's absences plus the vacant lines the FY2028 position control carries until each academy class graduates, the hours from the July 2025 academy class's first year; not FY2026's weeks with their own vacant lines, and not the unit's average availability.
lineage.stump: A competent solver executes the standard and rates a relief position at the title's average officer (32.4 to 35.3 hours on post a week), filing 63 positions, three short; the positions are filled from the July 2027 entry classes, and the July 2025 classes' first year (7.8 per cent off post against 14.5) puts a holder at 36.7 to 37.0 hours, so 59 are placed and one returns to the reserve.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-27 at the portal: both top responses landed the call (59 of 60, one returned) by rating the relief positions at the July 2025 entry classes' first-year off-post share, the Director's memo having named the July 2027 entry classes; the world screened for a new step the same day and set aside, the axes then banned (government_agency, budget_or_appropriation, research_desk, filed_standard)
